objective.statement: Read and write groups of 5, 6, 7 and 9 notes played in the time of 4 or 8.
successCriteria: I can say how much time an irregular group takes.
I choose the written value that fits the time.
I check the group's ratio apart from the bar total.

explanation.text: You already know the triplet: three equal notes played in the time normally taken by two. Other irregular divisions work the same way. A quintuplet puts five notes into the time of four, a sextuplet six into the time of four, a septuplet seven into the time of four, and a nonuplet nine into the time of eight. The number printed over the group is the number of notes.

music.textAlternative: A bar of 5/4: a quintuplet of five semiquavers, then four crotchets.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: a group of 5 of semiquaver, semiquaver, semiquaver, semiquaver, semiquaver, crotchet, crotchet, crotchet, crotchet.

explanation.caption: Five semiquavers take the time of one crotchet, so the bar still adds up to five crotchets.

explanation.text: The written value depends on the time the group must fit. Five, six or seven notes in the time of a crotchet are written as semiquavers (two beams). Five, six or seven notes in the time of a quaver are written as demisemiquavers (three beams). Nine notes in the time of a crotchet are written as demisemiquavers; nine in the time of a minim are written as semiquavers.

To work out how long a group lasts, imagine the ordinary notes it replaces. Five semiquavers in the time of four semiquavers last as long as four semiquavers: one crotchet. Check this separately from the bar total: first the group's length, then whether the bar adds up. The same counting works for dotted notes and ties: write every note as a number of the smallest value and add. A dotted crotchet is three quavers or twelve demisemiquavers, and a dotted crotchet tied to a quaver is four quavers.
Name the group (the number of notes), say what it replaces (the time of 4, or of 8), then say how long that is.

provenance.notes: Original wording. First Steps Grade 5 section 2 (pp. 106-107, read in the PDF): triplet as the simplest irregular division; 5, 6, 7 in the time of 4; 9 in the time of 8; written values adjust with the time they must fit. The nonuplet in the time of a minim is the book's 9-in-8 case.
